assumptions: The primary platform is Web/Desktop (laptops/desktops) since meeting notes are typically typed.
Meeting notes contain rich text (paragraphs, headings, lists, tasks) rather than heavy binary attachments like video or long audio in the MVP.
Synchronization happens via the internet using a centralized relay/backup database when online, rather than P2P local network discovery.
A simple shared workspace/document model is sufficient for the MVP instead of fine-grained role-based access control.
candidates: CRDTs (Conflict-free Replicated Data Types) like Yjs or Automerge for automatic and safe text merging.
Centralized synchronization server (e.g., Yjs websocket provider, Liveblocks, or custom Go/Node relay) to mediate syncing.
IndexedDB (Dexie.js / RxDB) for browser-based offline local storage, or SQLite (via Tauri/WASM) for desktop.
TipTap or Lexical rich text editors integrated with Yjs for a smooth WYSIWYG experience.
confirmed: The application is a team meeting notes application.
The application must be local-first, default storing data locally.
The application must support offline editing.
Upon reconnecting, offline modifications must sync and merge with team members' content.
The sync process must not easily overwrite others' changes.
conflicts: Offline Edit Freedom vs Strict Access Control: Ensuring users can edit offline conflicts with preventing unauthorized edits in real-time.
Automatic Merge vs Content Coherence: Automatically merging text ensures no overwrites but can lead to unreadable sentences if edits overlap closely.

gaps.dependency: User confirmation on whether automatic merge is always acceptable or if visual revision comparison is needed.
gaps.impact: Without a version history or diff view, users may feel they lost control when automatic merges make unexpected edits.
gaps.reason: CRDTs merge text cleanly at the byte level, but semantic changes may still clash (e.g., two people editing the same sentence).

gaps.dependency: Design of token-based authentication valid for offline usage.
gaps.impact: If tokens last too long, deactivated users can edit documents offline; if too short, valid offline users cannot edit.
gaps.reason: Local-first systems struggle with instant revocation without online validation.

options.impact: Uses Yjs/Automerge, low user friction, high development velocity.
options.label: (Recommended) Seamless automatic merging (CRDT-based) with a 'Version History' panel to inspect and restore past changes.

options.impact: Maximum control, high friction, slower user flow.
options.label: Manual review/approval flow (Git-like) where offline edits are treated as proposals.

questions.question: How should conflict resolution behave when offline edits overlap? Do you want seamless automatic merging (like Google Docs) or a visual version comparison/approval flow?
questions.reason: Determines the synchronization and data structures (CRDTs vs custom version logs).
questions.recommendation: (Recommended) Seamless automatic merging (CRDT-based) with a 'Version History' panel to inspect and restore past changes.
questions.recommendation_reason: Provides the best balance between ease of use and safety, avoiding the high friction of Git-like manual merging for non-developers.

options.impact: Easier to implement, supports remote teams, reliable cloud backup.
options.label: (Recommended) Centralized secure cloud relay (e.g., WebSocket sync server) with local caching.

options.impact: Complete privacy and works without internet, but connection reliability is highly dependent on local network configurations.
options.label: Pure local network P2P (mDNS/LAN discovery) sync directly between devices.

questions.question: Where should the synchronization occur? Over the public internet via a secure cloud coordinator, or locally via peer-to-peer (LAN/Wi-Fi) without internet?
questions.reason: Defines network requirements and connection reliability.
questions.recommendation: (Recommended) Centralized secure cloud relay (e.g., WebSocket sync server) with local caching.
questions.recommendation_reason: Vastly simplifies network traversal (NAT/firewalls) and ensures data is backed up, while working offline locally.

risks: CRDT history state bloat over time leading to high memory usage and slow loading on local client devices.
Security vulnerabilities where offline edits from unauthorized/revoked users are merged into the document because verification can only happen after reconnection.
Coherence issues where automated character-by-character merging results in grammatically incorrect or overlapping sentences.
unknowns: Whether real-time collaboration (collaborative editing when online) is required, or if async version-control editing is preferred.
Whether end-to-end encryption (E2EE) is a requirement for meeting notes security.
How offline user authentication and token expiration should be handled when keys are revoked during offline periods.
